analysis.title: Who Funds The Data Center Pipeline Now That Junk Buyers Have Left The Building?
key_insights: Goldman's Miriam Wheeler (global head of leveraged finance, Capital Solutions Group) says non-IG AI data center supply has contracted dramatically since end of September, with no new deals in the last month. About 30 AI deals came to market over the prior 12 months, roughly one every other week and sometimes weekly during the summer.

AI-related USD high yield spreads have widened to roughly 425bp versus about 265bp for non-AI BB/B. AI paper traded tighter than the rest of junk going into 2026. AI-related IG spreads are around 140bp, roughly 40bp wide of non-AI IG.

Early in 2026 high yield investors were underexposed to AI and spreads were near all-time tights, so most deals priced at 6% to 7% all-in yield without significant differentiation. Supply fears followed, with the market at one point expecting $60bn of issuance this fall, and investors have become more selective on project-level risk as the political backdrop changed.

Data center deals with a non-IG tenant plus an IG tenant wrap or residual value guarantee only gain IG-like credit risk upon completion of the facility. Developers typically have a 180-day grace period for late delivery, after which the tenant has a termination option. The tail risk is an extended multi-year delay in a pioneering market (West Texas rather than Northern Virginia) where re-tenanting is more complicated.
Per Zero Hedge's tally, only 468MW of the roughly 4GW financed by AI junk bonds had been delivered as of mid-October, leaving about 3.6GW undelivered with 180-day clocks running.
Texas is first on Wheeler's watch list because the Governor-Elect has discussed a data center moratorium. The Texas legislature does not adjourn until May 31, 2027.

Chips account for about 75% of a typical data center's cost and the shell and power about 25%. The volume of hardware needing financing could pressure spreads. Wheeler favors GPU-backed facilities (3-5 year weighted average life, fully amortizing, often contracted IG-tenant cash flows, escrow until delivery).

Refinancing mismatch: facilities sit on 15- to 20-year leases while the financing bonds often mature in five years. Rates and spreads are higher than when most deals priced, so higher leverage and tighter debt service coverage could limit new lending.

Wheeler sees winners and losers but no systemic contagion, expects the high yield market to stay open, and expects bifurcation to be the defining theme. Developers with unproven track records, limited equity or inferior leases will likely struggle to access capital, and structural complexity should come out of the market.

Bifurcation at the top: CoreWeave's debt was under heavy stress a few weeks ago while Microsoft's debt raise the following week was 5x oversubscribed (Goldman's Eric Sheridan). CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator said the company will not use the unsecured debt market at current yields and plans an investment-grade-rated delayed-draw loan at an implied 7-7.5%. CoreWeave is the tenant on seven of the 20 junk data center bonds.

Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam says saturation is the binding constraint: hyperscalers have issued $296 billion of debt this year versus Goldman's $250 billion forecast, and total AI-related debt issuance is $687 billion, with roughly 60% from non-hyperscalers.

Wheeler argues the supply slowdown may be constructive. Projects losing a lease or permit are likely shelved, which removes capacity permanently and means no large backlog is building, so existing supply becomes more valuable. Zero Hedge counters that this implies bonds backed by unfinished shells are the ones at risk.

Wheeler favors them for 3-5 year weighted average life, full amortization, contracted IG-tenant cash flows and escrow until delivery.

risk_factors: Delivery delays beyond the 180-day grace period give tenants a termination option, and IG wraps only take effect on completion.
A Texas data center moratorium or permitting delays could strand projects in West Texas, where re-tenanting analysis is more complicated.
Refinancing risk: 15-20 year leases against bonds that often mature in five years, with rates and spreads higher than at pricing.
Chips are about 75% of project cost, creating a large volume of hardware financing that could pressure spreads.
Supply saturation: $687 billion of AI-related debt issued this year.
About 3.6GW of the roughly 4GW financed by junk bonds was undelivered as of mid-October.
charts_described: Goldman spread charts show AI-related USD high yield spreads at roughly 425bp versus non-AI BB/B at roughly 265bp, with AI paper having traded tighter than the rest of junk going into 2026.
Goldman chart shows AI-related IG spreads at around 140bp, roughly 40bp wide of non-AI IG.
vol_and_positioning: High yield investors began 2026 underexposed to AI with spreads near all-time tights. Supply fears then drove spread widening, with the market at one point expecting $60bn of issuance this fall.
Demand for top-tier credit remains strong (Microsoft raise 5x oversubscribed), while weaker names face stress (CoreWeave).
geopolitical: Texas Governor-Elect has discussed a data center moratorium, and the Texas legislature does not adjourn until May 31, 2027.
A changed political backdrop (Democrats seeking to freeze the buildout, per prior Zero Hedge coverage) has made investors focus more on project-level risk.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Eric Sheridan: CoreWeave's debt under heavy stress while Microsoft's debt raise the following week was 5x oversubscribed.
Social Capital's Chamath Palihapitiya, in the same Goldman report, flags a duration mismatch for neoclouds that fund long-dated obligations with short-term revenue.

tension_points.bull_case: Wheeler expects the high yield market to stay open, sees no systemic contagion, and says secular compute demand is too large with supply not caught up. Hyperscalers remain extremely short on compute, so tenants are likely to work with late developers, and the supply slowdown makes existing supply more valuable.
tension_points.bear_case: Zero Hedge argues about 3.6GW of the roughly 4GW financed is undelivered with 180-day clocks running, IG wrappers only apply on completion, and a Texas moratorium could strand projects. CoreWeave, the tenant on 7 of 20 junk bonds, is refusing the unsecured market.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A project missing the 180-day outside date and the tenant exercising its termination option, or a Texas data center moratorium.
